messages.content: The DC trip is off my plate, and now I have a Raleigh client visit coming up in May. Can you help me frame it before I send anything for approval?
Sure. What dates are they asking for, and do you already know whether this is at the hospital campus or an office site?

Tentatively Monday May 12 through Thursday May 15. Tuesday and Wednesday are onsite build sessions. Thursday is probably a closeout, but I don't know the exact end time yet. They have not confirmed whether we're downtown at the hospital or at a suburban admin office.

That site detail matters for the hotel and ground transportation. For flights, ATL to RDU is straightforward: I would frame Monday as a late-morning or early-afternoon nonstop into Raleigh-Durham, then Thursday return after the closeout window is confirmed.
Do we need to look at connecting flights if they're cheaper?

I would not lead with a connection here. The one-stop options I see are only modestly cheaper and add a transfer on a short route. Unless your approval team requires the absolute lowest fare, a nonstop is the cleaner recommendation.
Agreed. I don't want to route through Charlotte or somewhere just to save a small amount.

For hotels, I would hold off on booking until the client confirms the site. If it is downtown, look near the hospital/city center so mornings are easy and dinner is walkable or on-site. If it is a suburban office, the better choice may be near that office or a North Hills/RTP-style area, depending on whether they expect visitors to use rideshare or rent cars.
If it's downtown, I'd rather not rent a car. I just need a hotel with solid reviews and somewhere reasonable to eat after work.

Then the downtown version would be: nonstop flight, hotel with a good guest rating, on-site or nearby dinner, and rideshare from RDU plus short rides or walking to the campus. The suburban version needs one extra decision: rideshare every day versus rental car.
Can you list what I need to ask the client before I bother my manager?

Ask them four things: exact worksite address, first required onsite time Tuesday, expected Thursday wrap-up time, and whether visitors normally use rideshare, shuttle, or rental cars between RDU, the hotel, and the site.
Great. Give me a tentative plan I can share internally, but mark it as not ready to book.

Tentative Raleigh plan, not ready to book: travel Monday May 12 to Thursday May 15 for solo client go-live prep. Preferred flight structure is ATL-RDU nonstop Monday late morning or early afternoon, with a Thursday return timed after the client confirms the closeout. Hotel choice depends on worksite: downtown hotel if the hospital campus is confirmed, with strong reviews and easy dinner access; suburban hotel or possible rental-car review if the admin office is confirmed. Missing approval details: exact address, Tuesday start time, Thursday end time, and local transportation expectation.

messages.content: Raleigh update: the client confirmed the downtown hospital campus. Tuesday starts at 8:30 a.m., Wednesday is a full working session, and Thursday closeout should finish by 12:30 p.m. Can we pick the flight and hotel package for approval?

Yes. That removes the biggest uncertainty. Do you want to arrive Monday with time to check in and prep, and is your manager okay with a slightly higher package if the cheaper option creates a bad schedule?
Exactly. I want a prep block Monday afternoon. There's no hard cap, but I need a clear reason if we don't pick the cheapest.

For flights, these are the practical choices with current round-trip estimates: Option A: nonstop ATL-RDU Monday 10:42 a.m.-12:04 p.m., return Thursday 5:40 p.m.-7:04 p.m., about $336. Best balance. Option B: same Monday outbound, Thursday 3:05 p.m.-4:28 p.m., about $318. Cheaper but tight after closeout. Option C: one-stop Monday 1:15 p.m.-5:05 p.m. via CLT, Thursday nonstop return, about $286. Cheapest, but it burns the Monday prep window and adds connection risk.
Is there any reason to leave Atlanta earlier Monday?

There are earlier nonstops, but they do not add much value here. A very early departure gets you to Raleigh before most hotel rooms are ready and makes Monday morning rushed. The 10:42 a.m. outbound still gives you lunch, check-in or bag drop, and a useful prep block.
What about that 3:05 return? Could I make it if the closeout ends at 12:30?

You probably could if everything ends on time and you leave almost immediately. But it leaves little room for a late question, a badge checkout delay, lunch, or downtown traffic. The 5:40 p.m. return gives you a real buffer without turning into a late-night arrival.
Then don't save $18 just to make Thursday stressful. Show me the hotel choices.

For May 12-15, the strongest hotel set is: Raleigh Marriott City Center: about $239/night before taxes, guest rating around 4.3, downtown, on-site dining, paid breakfast, easy rideshare to the hospital campus. Hampton Inn & Suites Raleigh Midtown: about $207/night, rating around 4.4, breakfast included, but a less convenient morning ride to the campus. Hyatt Place RDU/Airport area: about $163/night, rating around 4.1, breakfast included, lowest rate, but both onsite mornings become longer and less predictable.
I like included breakfast, but I don't want to make both mornings harder for this trip.

That points toward the downtown Marriott despite paid breakfast. The savings at Midtown or the airport are real, but they are partly offset by extra rideshare time and less flexibility before an 8:30 start.
Any downtown option with included breakfast and good ratings?

There is a Residence Inn downtown with included breakfast and a rating around 4.4, but it is pricing closer to $271/night. It also has nearby restaurants rather than the same full on-site dining setup. For a solo three-night work stay, I would not pay the extra unless the kitchenette or included breakfast is important enough to you.
No kitchenette needed. The Marriott sounds more straightforward.

Then I would send Option A for approval: nonstop late-morning outbound, early-evening Thursday return, and Raleigh Marriott City Center. It is not the cheapest package, but it protects the Monday prep block and the Thursday closeout buffer while keeping the hotel close to the confirmed downtown site.
Can you phrase the manager justification? Especially why not the airport hotel.

Draft justification: Recommend ATL-RDU nonstops May 12-15 with the Thursday 5:40 p.m. return to allow a buffer after the 12:30 p.m. client closeout. Recommend Raleigh Marriott City Center because the client confirmed the downtown hospital campus and Tuesday begins at 8:30 a.m. The airport hotel is cheaper, but it adds longer rides both onsite mornings and increases commute uncertainty. No rental car is planned; rideshare should cover airport and campus transfers.
Looks good. Anything missing before I send it?

Only two booking checks after approval: confirm the Marriott rate is still cancellable, and confirm the client is comfortable with rideshare rather than rental car. Otherwise, send this package: Monday 10:42 a.m. nonstop outbound, Thursday 5:40 p.m. nonstop return, Raleigh Marriott City Center for three nights, paid breakfast noted, no rental car planned.

Added the quiet room request away from elevators. I also noted no rental car: rideshare from RDU to the hotel, rideshare or short downtown transfer to the hospital campus, and rideshare back to RDU Thursday afternoon.
Any breakfast fallback for Tuesday before the 8:30 start?

Yes. The hotel coffee option should work for a quick paid breakfast, and there are early cafes nearby if you want something lighter. For the first onsite morning, plan to leave the hotel around 7:55 a.m. so you have time for security or badge pickup before 8:30.
Where are the receipts going?

I saved the flight and hotel receipts to your Raleigh May go-live prep folder and emailed copies to your work address. The reimbursement note includes: flight $336.20, hotel estimated $823.77, breakfast not included, no rental car, rideshare expected.
Anything else before I close the loop with the client?

Close-loop checklist: send the client your Monday arrival and Thursday departure windows, ask for badge or visitor instructions, confirm the Tuesday room/location on the downtown campus, and keep the Thursday 12:30 closeout assumption visible. Travel follow-ups are online check-in, rechecking seat assignments, and saving rideshare receipts during the trip.
